proof_text:
For the indexed union, $x \in \bigcup_{i \in \emptyset} A_i$ requires
the existence of an index $i \in \emptyset$ such that $x \in A_i$.
Because $\emptyset$ contains no indices, this existential condition is
unconditionally false for every $x \in U$, yielding the empty set
$\emptyset$. For the indexed intersection,
$x \in \bigcap_{i \in \emptyset} A_i$ requires that for all
$i \in \emptyset$, $x \in A_i$. Because the antecedent
$i \in \emptyset$ is false, the conditional implication is vacuously
true for every element $x \in U$. Consequently, every element of the
ambient universe $U$ satisfies the definition, yielding $U$.

Theorem:
given:
. I, U is \set
. A(i__) is \function:on{I}:to{\power.set:of{U}}
where: I = \empty.set
then:
. \indexed.union:of{A}:over{I}:in{U} = \empty.set
. \indexed.intersection:of{A}:over{I}:in{U} = U
Documented:
. called: "Empty Indexed Union and Intersection"
. description: "The union of an empty family is empty, while its intersection is
                the explicitly supplied ambient universe."
